key_findings.finding: The primary and directly relevant study is PMID 25092649 (Toxicological Sciences, 2014), titled “AMP-activated protein kinase deficiency rescues paraquat-induced cardiac contractile dysfunction through an autophagy-dependent mechanism.” In wild-type mice, paraquat (45 mg/kg for 48 h) caused impaired echocardiographic function, depressed cardiomyocyte shortening and Ca2+ handling, reduced survival, and mitochondrial membrane-potential loss; paraquat also increased AMPK phosphorylation and autophagy markers. These effects were attenuated—not worsened—by reduced AMPK activity in transgenic mice overexpressing kinase-dead AMPKα2, with reduced activity of both AMPKα1 and α2.

Thus, the reported direction is paraquat → AMPK/autophagy activation → cardiac contractile injury, while AMPK deficiency/inhibition → less autophagy signaling and preserved contractility.
